note: Attacker-controlled UCS-4 input enters the ASCII conversion path as the domain label to be transformed.
The input label is copied into a heap buffer sized from the caller-provided length, preserving the attacker-controlled content for later conversion.
The UCS-4 attacker input is converted to UTF-8; the resulting byte string remains derived from the original malicious label.
The UTF-8 attacker input is passed into the lookup/encoding pipeline, which may produce an ACE output string.
Root-cause sink: the function copies the produced output into a caller-supplied fixed buffer with strcpy, so an oversized attacker-triggered output can overflow memory and crash the target.
